source.text: וְאָ֣הַבְתָּ֔ אֵ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֣ מִשְׁמַרְתּ֗וֹ וְחֻקֹּתָ֧יו וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֛יו וּמִצְוֺתָ֖יו כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will love Yahweh your God and keep his charge and his statutes and his judgments and his commandments all the days.

en.L: And you shall love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} charge and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} judgments and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments all the days.
en.B: So love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and always keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} requirements, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} statutes, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rulings, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments.
en.R: So love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Always do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asks of you, and obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws, rules, and commands.

decisions.choice: So you shall love: the conclusion drawn from what the LORD has done
decisions.reason: The verse begins with "and" and a verb that looks forward: you will love, that is, you are to love. It draws the conclusion of 10:12-22. Because the LORD is great and has done great things for Israel, Israel is to love him and keep his commands. Love here is loyalty to the covenant, shown in obedience, as in 6:5 and 10:12.

decisions.choice: his charge: what he has given you to keep, your duty toward him
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "keep" just before it, so the phrase is literally "keep his keeping". It means a duty or charge entrusted to someone, and is used of the Levites' duties at the tabernacle (Numbers 3:7-8). Here it sums up everything the LORD requires. Genesis 26:5 joins it to commandments, statutes and laws in the same way, of Abraham.

decisions.choice: all the days: always, for as long as you live
decisions.reason: "All the days" means at all times, without end (4:40; 5:29).

decisions.choice: requirements (Balanced); do what he asks of you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "charge". Balanced and Readable say what the charge is, since "keep his charge" is not plain modern English.

source.text: וִֽידַעְתֶּם֮ הַיּוֹם֒ כִּ֣י׀לֹ֣א אֶת־בְּנֵיכֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־יָדְעוּ֙ וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־רָא֔וּ אֶת־מוּסַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם אֶת־גָּדְל֕וֹ אֶת־יָדוֹ֙ הַחֲזָקָ֔ה וּזְרֹע֖וֹ הַנְּטוּיָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And know today, for not your sons who have not known and who have not seen, the discipline of Yahweh your God, his greatness, his hand the strong and his arm the outstretched,

en.L: And know today — for [I speak] not [to] your {{gender:children|sons}} who have not known and who have not seen — the discipline of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strong hand and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} outstretched arm,
en.B: Recognize today — for it is not your {{gender:children|sons}} I am speaking to, who have neither known nor seen it — the discipline of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} greatness, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty hand and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} outstretched arm,
en.R: Today you must take to heart how {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God trained you. I am not talking to your {{gender:children|sons}}. They never knew these things or saw them. But you saw how great {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is and how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mighty power.

decisions.choice: discipline: training by what God did, both correction and care
decisions.reason: The word means teaching, training or correction, the kind a father gives a son (8:5; Proverbs 3:11-12). It covers everything listed in verses 3-6: the plagues on Egypt, the rescue at the sea, the years in the wilderness and the punishment of Dathan and Abiram. Through all of it the LORD was teaching Israel who he is.

decisions.choice: a break in the sentence: "know" waits for its object until after the words about the children
decisions.reason: Moses begins "know today", stops to say that he is not speaking to the children, then names what they are to know, "the discipline of the LORD". The sentence runs on through verse 6 and is finished by verse 7: it is you, not your children, whose eyes saw it. The point is that the hearers are witnesses.

decisions.choice: you, not your children: those who saw the exodus as young people
decisions.reason: The adults who left Egypt had died in the wilderness (2:14-16), but those who were children or young then had seen the plagues and the sea with their own eyes. Moses speaks to them as eyewitnesses, unlike their own children, born in the wilderness, who know these events only by hearing about them.

decisions.choice: strong hand and outstretched arm: God's power at work
decisions.reason: The pair describes the LORD acting with force to rescue Israel from Egypt, as in 4:34, 5:15 and 7:19.

decisions.choice: [I speak] not [to] (Literal); it is not ... I am speaking to (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "not your children". Literal brackets the words English needs; Balanced keeps the break in the sentence with dashes.

decisions.choice: three short sentences; mighty power
decisions.reason: Readable puts the main point first and splits the long sentence, which in the Hebrew runs on to verse 7. It says "mighty power" for the strong hand and outstretched arm.

source.text: וְאֶת־אֹֽתֹתָיו֙ וְאֶֽת־מַעֲשָׂ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה בְּת֣וֹךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם לְפַרְעֹ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֖יִם וּלְכָל־אַרְצֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: and his signs and his deeds which he did in [the] midst of Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his land,

en.L: and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} signs and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did in the midst of Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his land,
en.B: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} signs and the deeds {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did in Egypt to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his whole land,
en.R: You saw the signs and the great things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did in Egypt to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and to his whole country.

decisions.choice: his signs and his deeds: the plagues on Egypt
decisions.reason: The signs are the plagues of Exodus 7-12, acts that showed who the LORD is (Exodus 7:3-5; 10:1-2). "His deeds" are the same events seen as the works of his power.

decisions.choice: You saw ... the great things
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence with "You saw", picking up verse 2, and says "great things" for the deeds, as verse 7 calls them "great".

source.text: וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂה֩ לְחֵ֨יל מִצְרַ֜יִם לְסוּסָ֣יו וּלְרִכְבּ֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר הֵצִ֜יף אֶת־מֵ֤י יַם־סוּף֙ עַל־פְּנֵיהֶ֔ם בְּרָדְפָ֖ם אַחֲרֵיכֶ֑ם וַיְאַבְּדֵ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and what he did to [the] army of Egypt, to its horses and to its chariotry, that he made flow [the] water of [the] Sea of Reeds over their faces when they pursued after you, and destroyed them Yahweh until this day,

en.L: and what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did to the army of Egypt, to its horses and to its chariots, how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the water of the Sea of Reeds flow over their faces as they pursued after you, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed them to this day,
en.B: what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did to the Egyptian army, its horses and its chariots, how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the waters of the Red Sea flow over them as they chased you, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed them, and they are gone to this day,
en.R: You saw what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did to the army of Egypt with its horses and chariots. They chased you, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the water of the Red Sea cover them. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} destroyed them, and they have never recovered.

decisions.choice: made the water flow over them: the sea closing over Egypt's army
decisions.reason: This recalls Exodus 14:26-28 and 15:4-10. The verb means to make water overflow or flood, so that the army was covered.

decisions.choice: Sea of Reeds: the sea Israel crossed, known as the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name means "sea of reeds". It is the same body of water as in Exodus 13:18 and 15:4, traditionally called the Red Sea; its exact place is not known for certain.

decisions.choice: destroyed them to this day: wiped them out for good
decisions.reason: "To this day" means that the defeat was final: Egypt's army never came after Israel again, and the effect lasts to the time Moses speaks.

decisions.choice: Red Sea
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the familiar name, as in Exodus; Literal keeps "Sea of Reeds".

source.text: וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר עַד־בֹּאֲכֶ֖ם עַד־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and what he did for you in the wilderness until your coming to this place,

en.L: and what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place,
en.B: what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did for you in the wilderness until you arrived at this place,
en.R: You saw what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did for you in the desert until you came to this place.

decisions.choice: for you: his care in the wilderness, which also tested you
decisions.reason: The words can mean "to you" or "for you". In the wilderness the LORD fed Israel with manna, kept their clothes from wearing out, and tested and trained them (8:2-5). Both care and testing belong to the "discipline" of verse 2.

decisions.choice: this place: the plains of Moab, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Moses speaks in the land of Moab across from Jericho, where Israel camped before crossing the Jordan (1:5; 3:29).

source.text: וַאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה לְדָתָ֣ן וְלַאֲבִירָ֗ם בְּנֵ֣י אֱלִיאָב֮ בֶּן־רְאוּבֵן֒ אֲשֶׁ֨ר פָּצְתָ֤ה הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֶת־פִּ֔יהָ וַתִּבְלָעֵ֥ם וְאֶת־בָּתֵּיהֶ֖ם וְאֶת־אָהֳלֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־הַיְקוּם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּרַגְלֵיהֶ֔ם בְּקֶ֖רֶב כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: and what he did to Dathan and to Abiram, [the] sons of Eliab son of Reuben, when opened the earth its mouth and swallowed them and their households and their tents and all the living [thing] which [was] at their feet, in [the] midst of all Israel,

en.L: and what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did to Dathan and to Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households and their tents and every living thing that [was] at their feet, in the midst of all Israel,
en.B: and what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab son of Reuben, when the earth opened its mouth in the middle of all Israel and swallowed them, with their households, their tents, and every living thing that belonged to them,
en.R: You saw what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, from the tribe of Reuben. While all Israel was there, the ground opened up like a mouth and swallowed them. It swallowed their families, their tents, and every living thing they owned.

decisions.choice: Dathan and Abiram: the Reubenites who rose against Moses
decisions.reason: The story is told in Numbers 16:1-35. Dathan and Abiram refused Moses' summons and accused him of making himself a ruler (Numbers 16:12-14). Korah, who led the same revolt, is not named here; the focus is on the two men and their households, whom the earth swallowed (Numbers 16:27-33).

decisions.choice: son of Reuben: descendant of Reuben
decisions.reason: Eliab was the son of Pallu, Reuben's son (Numbers 26:5-9), so "son" here means descendant: they belonged to the tribe of Reuben.

decisions.choice: every living thing at their feet: all the people and animals that followed them
decisions.reason: "At the feet" of someone means following them or belonging to them (Exodus 11:8; Judges 4:10). The word for "living thing" means whatever stands or lives, and covers both people and livestock (Genesis 7:4, 23).

decisions.choice: that belonged to them (Balanced); they owned (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "at their feet"; Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: from the tribe of Reuben
decisions.reason: Readable says "from the tribe of Reuben", following meaning decision m2, since Eliab was not Reuben's own son.

source.text: כִּ֤י עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ הָֽרֹאֹ֔ת אֶת־כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה הַגָּדֹ֑ל אֲשֶׁ֖ר עָשָֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: for your eyes [are] the ones seeing all [the] work of Yahweh the great which he did.

en.L: for your eyes [are] the ones seeing all the great work of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did.
en.B: for it is your own eyes that have seen all the great work that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done.
en.R: With your own eyes you saw all the great things {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done.

decisions.choice: for your eyes saw: the end of the sentence that began in verse 2
decisions.reason: The words finish the thought broken off in verse 2: not your children, but you, saw these things. The stress falls on "your eyes", the hearers as eyewitnesses (4:3, 9; 10:21).

decisions.choice: all the great work: every act listed in verses 3-6, taken as one
decisions.reason: "Work" is singular. Moses sums up the plagues, the sea, the wilderness and the judgment on Dathan and Abiram as one great work of the LORD.

decisions.choice: all the great things
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plural, which is more natural in plain English; the meaning is the same.

source.text: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּם֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַמִּצְוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֛ר אָנֹכִ֥י מְצַוְּךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם לְמַ֣עַן תֶּחֶזְק֗וּ וּבָאתֶם֙ וִֽירִשְׁתֶּ֣ם אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֛ם עֹבְרִ֥ים שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will keep all the commandment which I [am] commanding you today, so that you may be strong and go in and take possession of the land which you [are] crossing over there to possess it,

en.L: And you shall keep all the commandment that I [am] commanding you today, so that you may be strong, and go in and take possession of the land that you are crossing over into to take possession of it,
en.B: So keep the whole commandment that I am giving you today, so that you may have strength to go in and take possession of the land you are crossing over to possess,
en.R: So obey every command I am giving you today. Then you will be strong enough to go in and take over the land. You are about to cross the Jordan River to make it your own.

decisions.choice: all the commandment: the whole charge as one
decisions.reason: "Commandment" is singular, as in 5:31, 6:1 and 8:1. It names the whole of what Moses teaches in the LORD's name, taken as a single charge, not one law among many.

decisions.choice: so that you may be strong: obedience as the way to strength
decisions.reason: Keeping the commandment is what will make Israel strong enough to take the land. The same verb is used in the charge to Joshua to "be strong" (31:7; Joshua 1:6-7).

decisions.choice: take possession of: receive the land as your own
decisions.reason: The verb means to take over and hold something as an inheritance. It is used of the land, which Israel is to receive from the LORD (1:8).

decisions.choice: the Jordan River
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "crossing over there". Readable names the river, as verse 31 does.

source.text: וּלְמַ֨עַן תַּאֲרִ֤יכוּ יָמִים֙ עַל־הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁבַּ֨ע יְהוָ֧ה לַאֲבֹתֵיכֶ֛ם לָתֵ֥ת לָהֶ֖ם וּלְזַרְעָ֑ם אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָֽשׁ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and so that you may prolong days on the land which swore Yahweh to your fathers to give to them and to their offspring, a land flowing [with] milk and honey.

en.L: and so that you may prolong [your] days on the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your fathers to give to them and to their offspring, a land flowing [with] milk and honey.
en.B: and so that you may live long in the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your ancestors to give to them and to their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
en.R: Then you will live a long time in the land. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} promised with an oath to give it to your ancestors and their descendants. It is a land flowing with milk and honey.

decisions.choice: prolong days: live long
decisions.reason: To "lengthen days" on the land means to live there long and keep it, as in 4:40, 5:33 and 6:2.

decisions.choice: the land the LORD swore to your fathers: the promise to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
decisions.reason: The fathers are the ancestors to whom God promised the land by oath (Genesis 15:18; 26:3; 28:13; Deuteronomy 1:8).

decisions.choice: flowing with milk and honey: rich and fertile
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures a land with good pasture for herds and plenty of wild and cultivated sweetness, as in Exodus 3:8 and Numbers 13:27. The honey may be bees' honey or a syrup made from dates or grapes.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors" for "fathers", since the word means forebears; Literal keeps "fathers".

source.text: כִּ֣י הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתָּ֤ה בָא־שָׁ֨מָּה֙ לְרִשְׁתָּ֔הּ לֹ֣א כְאֶ֤רֶץ מִצְרַ֨יִם֙ הִ֔וא אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְצָאתֶ֖ם מִשָּׁ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר תִּזְרַע֙ אֶֽת־זַרְעֲךָ֔ וְהִשְׁקִ֥יתָ בְרַגְלְךָ֖ כְּגַ֥ן הַיָּרָֽק׃

records.literal_gloss: For the land which you [are] going there to possess it, not like [the] land of Egypt [is] it from which you came out from there, where you sowed your seed and watered [it] with your foot like a garden of the vegetable.

en.L: For the land that you are going into to take possession of it — it [is] not like the land of Egypt, from which you came out, where you would sow your seed and water [it] with your foot like a vegetable garden.
en.B: For the land you are entering to possess is not like the land of Egypt that you came out of, where you sowed your seed and watered it by foot, like a vegetable garden.
en.R: The land you are going into is not like Egypt, the land you left. There you planted your seed and then had to water it yourselves, using your feet to move the water through ditches, as people do in a vegetable garden.

decisions.choice: watered with your foot: irrigation by human labor
decisions.reason: Egypt has almost no rain; its fields were watered from the Nile through channels and ditches. "With your foot" most likely means opening and closing the small earth walls of the channels with the foot, or treading a device that lifted water. Either way, the water came by hard work, as in a vegetable garden watered by hand.

decisions.choice: you sowed: what you used to do
decisions.reason: The verb describes a repeated, habitual action: this is how farming was done in Egypt, where Israel had lived.

decisions.choice: using your feet to move the water through ditches
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture. Because the exact method is not certain (meaning decision m1), it names the most likely one.

source.text: וְהָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אַתֶּ֜ם עֹבְרִ֥ים שָׁ֨מָּה֙ לְרִשְׁתָּ֔הּ אֶ֥רֶץ הָרִ֖ים וּבְקָעֹ֑ת לִמְטַ֥ר הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם תִּשְׁתֶּה־מָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the land which you [are] crossing over there to possess it [is] a land of mountains and valleys; by [the] rain of the heavens it drinks water,

en.L: But the land that you are crossing over into to take possession of it [is] a land of mountains and valleys; it drinks water by the rain of the heavens,
en.B: But the land you are crossing over to possess is a land of hills and valleys, which drinks in water from the rain of the sky,
en.R: But the land you are about to enter has hills and valleys. Rain from the sky gives it the water it needs.

decisions.choice: by the rain of the heavens: water that comes from God, not from human work
decisions.reason: The land of Canaan depends on rain, which no farmer can make. Egypt's water came by labor (verse 10); this land's water comes from the sky, that is from the LORD, who gives or holds back the rain (verses 14 and 17).

decisions.choice: it drinks water: the ground soaks up the rain
decisions.reason: The land is pictured as drinking the rain it needs.

decisions.choice: hills
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word covers both mountains and hills. The high country of Canaan is mostly hills; Literal keeps "mountains".

source.text: אֶ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ דֹּרֵ֣שׁ אֹתָ֑הּ תָּמִ֗יד עֵינֵ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ בָּ֔הּ מֵֽרֵשִׁית֙ הַשָּׁנָ֔ה וְעַ֖ד אַחֲרִ֥ית שָׁנָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: a land which Yahweh your God [is] caring for it; continually the eyes of Yahweh your God [are] on it, from [the] beginning of the year and until [the] end of [the] year.

en.L: a land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God cares for; the eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God [are] continually on it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
en.B: a land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God cares for. The eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God are on it always, from the beginning of the year to its end.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God takes care of this land. He watches over it all year long, from the first day of the year to the last.

decisions.choice: cares for: looks after, attends to
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to seek or inquire. With the land as its object it means to look after it, to give it attention and care.

decisions.choice: his eyes are on it: he watches over it with care
decisions.reason: God's eyes on a place or person express his constant care for it (1 Kings 8:29; 9:3; Psalm 33:18).

decisions.choice: from the beginning of the year to its end: through the whole farming year
decisions.reason: The rains come in their seasons through the year (verse 14), from the autumn sowing to the spring harvest. The land needs the LORD's care in every season.

decisions.choice: He watches over it
decisions.reason: Readable makes the second clause a new sentence with God as its subject, saying what "his eyes are on it" means.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה אִם־שָׁמֹ֤עַ תִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל־מִצְוֺתַ֔י אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם לְאַהֲבָ֞ה אֶת־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶם֙ וּלְעָבְד֔וֹ בְּכָל־לְבַבְכֶ֖ם וּבְכָל־נַפְשְׁכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, if surely you will listen to my commandments which I [am] commanding you today, to love Yahweh your God and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,

en.L: And it will be, if you will indeed listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments that I am commanding you today, to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and to serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your soul,
en.B: If you truly obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commandments that I am giving you today, loving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God and serving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your soul,
en.R: So obey {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} commands carefully. I am giving them to you today. Love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with all your heart and with all your being.

decisions.choice: my commandments ... the LORD your God: Moses speaks the LORD's own words
alternatives: my: Moses' own commandments, with the LORD speaking only from verse 14
decisions.reason: In verses 13-15 the speaker says "my commandments" and "I will give the rain": the LORD speaks in the first person through Moses, even while the same sentence names "the LORD your God" in the third person. Moses' usual words "which I am commanding you today" show that he is the one delivering them. From verse 16 on, Moses speaks of the LORD again in the third person. "My" could also be Moses' own, since he often calls the commands his (verse 8), but verse 14 shows that the LORD is speaking here.

decisions.choice: surely listen: listen carefully, obey in earnest
decisions.reason: The verb "listen" is doubled for emphasis. To listen to commands means to obey them.

decisions.choice: with all your heart and all your soul: with your whole self
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of thought and will; the soul is the whole living person, with its desires and its life. Together they mean with everything you are, as in 6:5 and 10:12.

decisions.choice: being
decisions.reason: Readable says "being" for the Hebrew word, since "soul" can suggest only an inner, spiritual part of a person. Literal and Balanced keep "soul".

decisions.choice: So obey ... Love ... (commands, with the condition picked up in verse 14)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the long "if" clause into commands and states the condition at the start of verse 14 ("If you do").

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֧י מְטַֽר־אַרְצְכֶ֛ם בְּעִתּ֖וֹ יוֹרֶ֣ה וּמַלְק֑וֹשׁ וְאָסַפְתָּ֣ דְגָנֶ֔ךָ וְתִֽירֹשְׁךָ֖ וְיִצְהָרֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: and I will give [the] rain of your land in its season, early rain and late rain, and you will gather your grain and your new wine and your fresh oil.

en.L: then I will give the rain of your land in its season, the early rain and the late rain, and you will gather in your grain and your new wine and your fresh oil.
en.B: then I will give your land its rain at the right time, the autumn rain and the spring rain, and you will gather in your grain, your new wine, and your olive oil.
en.R: If you do, I will send rain on your land at the right time, in the fall and in the spring. Then you will gather in your grain, your grapes for new wine, and your olives for oil.

decisions.choice: I will give: the LORD speaks in the first person
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "I will give" here and in verse 15. The Samaritan Pentateuch and the ancient Greek translation read "he will give", in the third person, which smooths the change of speaker (see the note on verse 13). The Hebrew text is followed. Reviewers should check this against the textual evidence.

decisions.choice: early rain and late rain: the rains of autumn and spring
decisions.reason: The early rain falls in October and November and softens the ground for plowing and sowing; the late rain falls in March and April and fills out the grain before harvest. Summer is dry. If either rain failed, the harvest failed (Jeremiah 5:24; Joel 2:23).

decisions.choice: grain, new wine and fresh oil: the three main crops of the land
decisions.reason: The words name the harvest of the fields, the vineyards and the olive groves: grain, freshly pressed grape juice or new wine, and fresh olive oil. They often appear together as the gifts of the land (7:13; Hosea 2:10).

decisions.choice: the autumn rain and the spring rain (Balanced); in the fall and in the spring (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the seasons, following meaning decision m2; Literal keeps "early" and "late".

decisions.choice: your grapes for new wine, and your olives for oil
decisions.reason: Readable names the fruit from which wine and oil are made, since what is gathered in is the crop.

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֛י עֵ֥שֶׂב בְּשָׂדְךָ֖ לִבְהֶמְתֶּ֑ךָ וְאָכַלְתָּ֖ וְשָׂבָֽעְתָּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will give grass in your field for your cattle, and you will eat and be satisfied.

en.L: And I will give grass in your field for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.
en.B: I will provide grass in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat and be full.
en.R: I will make grass grow in your fields for your animals. And you will have all you want to eat.

decisions.choice: you will eat and be satisfied: the moment of danger
decisions.reason: The same words come in 6:11 and 8:10-12, each time followed by a warning: when you have plenty, do not forget the LORD. Verse 16 gives that warning here.

decisions.choice: I will make grass grow
decisions.reason: Readable says how God "gives" grass: by making it grow, through the rain of verse 14.

source.text: הִשָּֽׁמְר֣וּ לָכֶ֔ם פֶּ֥ן יִפְתֶּ֖ה לְבַבְכֶ֑ם וְסַרְתֶּ֗ם וַעֲבַדְתֶּם֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוִיתֶ֖ם לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Take heed to yourselves lest be deceived your heart and you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them,

en.L: Take care for yourselves, lest your heart be deceived and you turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them,
en.B: Be careful that your hearts are not led astray, so that you turn away and serve other gods and bow down to them,
en.R: But be careful! Do not let yourselves be fooled into turning away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to serve other gods and worship them.

decisions.choice: be deceived: be enticed, talked into something
decisions.reason: The verb means to be open to persuasion, to be lured or fooled (Job 31:27; Hosea 7:11, "a silly dove"). The danger is not open rebellion but being drawn away little by little.

decisions.choice: bow down: worship
decisions.reason: Bowing to the ground was the act of worship before a god, and the second commandment forbids it before any other god (5:9).

decisions.choice: other gods: the gods of Canaan, thought to give rain and harvest
decisions.reason: In the land the people would meet gods believed to send rain and make the ground fruitful. Moses has just said that the rain comes from the LORD (verses 11-14); serving other gods for it would be the deception.

decisions.choice: turning away from the LORD
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has only "turn aside". Readable says from whom, as verse 28 says "turn from the way".

source.text: וְחָרָ֨ה אַף־יְהוָ֜ה בָּכֶ֗ם וְעָצַ֤ר אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְלֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה מָטָ֔ר וְהָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה לֹ֥א תִתֵּ֖ן אֶת־יְבוּלָ֑הּ וַאֲבַדְתֶּ֣ם מְהֵרָ֗ה מֵעַל֙ הָאָ֣רֶץ הַטֹּבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and burn [the] anger of Yahweh against you, and he will shut up the heavens and there will not be rain, and the ground will not give its produce, and you will perish quickly from on the land the good which Yahweh [is] giving to you.

en.L: and the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burn against you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shut up the heavens so that there is no rain and the ground does not give its produce, and you perish quickly from upon the good land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is giving to you.
en.B: and the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blaze against you. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will shut up the sky so that there is no rain and the ground yields no crops, and you will quickly be wiped out from the good land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is giving you.
en.R: If you do, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will become very angry with you. He will stop the rain. Nothing will grow in your fields, and you will soon die and be gone from the good land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is giving you.

decisions.choice: the anger burns: fierce anger
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that the LORD's anger (literally his nose) grows hot. It is a picture of strong anger, as in 6:15 and 7:4.

decisions.choice: he will shut up the heavens: drought as the covenant's warning
decisions.reason: The sky is pictured as a store of rain that the LORD can close. Drought is one of the curses for breaking the covenant (28:23-24; Leviticus 26:19). Solomon's prayer (1 Kings 8:35) and the drought in Elijah's time (1 Kings 17:1) show it in later history.

decisions.choice: perish quickly from the land: be destroyed and lose the land
decisions.reason: The warning is of death and of losing the land itself, as in 4:26 and 8:19-20.

decisions.choice: Then he will shut up ... (a new sentence)
decisions.reason: Balanced ends the "lest" clause after the LORD's anger and begins a new sentence for what follows from it, to keep the sentence readable.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתֶּם֙ אֶת־דְּבָרַ֣י אֵ֔לֶּה עַל־לְבַבְכֶ֖ם וְעַֽל־נַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם וּקְשַׁרְתֶּ֨ם אֹתָ֤ם לְאוֹת֙ עַל־יֶדְכֶ֔ם וְהָי֥וּ לְטוֹטָפֹ֖ת בֵּ֥ין עֵינֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will put these words of mine on your heart and on your soul, and bind them for a sign on your hand, and they will be for frontlets between your eyes.

en.L: And you shall put these words of mine on your heart and on your soul, and you shall bind them for a sign on your hand, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes.
en.B: Fix these words of mine in your heart and in your soul. Tie them as a sign on your hand, and let them be a band between your eyes.
en.R: Keep these words of mine in your hearts and minds. Tie them on your hands as a sign, and wear them on your foreheads to remind you.

decisions.choice: these words of mine: Moses' teaching, as in 6:6-9
decisions.reason: Verses 18-20 repeat 6:6-9 almost word for word. There "these words" are those "I am commanding you today", Moses' teaching of the LORD's commands. Here "mine" is again best taken as Moses speaking in his own voice, though it could still be the LORD's voice of verses 13-15.

decisions.choice: frontlets: a band or mark on the forehead
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here, in 6:8 and in Exodus 13:16, and its meaning is not certain; see the note at Exodus 13:16. Later Jewish practice took these words literally and wore phylacteries, small boxes holding written passages, among them this one, on the arm and the forehead.

decisions.choice: on your heart and on your soul: learned, held inwardly
decisions.reason: To put words on the heart is to take them in and keep them in mind, so that they shape thought and will.

decisions.choice: a band between your eyes (Balanced); on your foreheads (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Exodus 13:16, Balanced says "band" and Readable says where it is worn; Literal keeps "frontlets between your eyes".

decisions.choice: minds
decisions.reason: Readable says "hearts and minds" for "heart and soul": in plain English that says that the words are to be held in the whole inner self.

source.text: וְלִמַּדְתֶּ֥ם אֹתָ֛ם אֶת־בְּנֵיכֶ֖ם לְדַבֵּ֣ר בָּ֑ם בְּשִׁבְתְּךָ֤ בְּבֵיתֶ֨ךָ֙ וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ֣ בַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וּֽבְשָׁכְבְּךָ֖ וּבְקוּמֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will teach them to your sons, speaking of them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road and when you lie down and when you rise.

en.L: And you shall teach them to your {{gender:children|sons}}, speaking of them when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road, and when you lie down and when you rise.
en.B: Teach them to your {{gender:children|sons}}, talking about them when you sit at home and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
en.R: Teach them to your {{gender:children|sons}}. Talk about them when you are at home and when you are out on the road, when you go to bed and when you get up.

decisions.choice: sitting and walking, lying down and rising: at all times and everywhere
decisions.reason: The two pairs cover the whole of life, at home and away, night and morning, as in 6:7.

decisions.choice: speaking of them: teaching by talking about them
decisions.reason: In 6:7 the parent is told "you shall speak of them". Here the form "by speaking" says how the teaching is done: in ordinary talk through the day.

decisions.choice: your sons: your children, daughters as well as sons
decisions.reason: The word is "sons", but the teaching is for the next generation as a whole, as in 4:9-10.

source.text: וּכְתַבְתָּ֛ם עַל־מְזוּז֥וֹת בֵּיתֶ֖ךָ וּבִשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will write them on [the] doorposts of your house and on your gates,

en.L: And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
en.B: Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
en.R: Write them on the doorframes of your houses and on your town gates.

decisions.choice: doorposts and gates: the entrances of home and town
decisions.reason: The doorposts are the side frames of a house door; "your gates" are the gates of the town, where people met, traded and held court. The words are to mark both private and public life. Later Jewish practice fixes a small case holding these passages to the doorpost (the mezuzah, the Hebrew word for doorpost).

decisions.choice: your town gates
decisions.reason: Readable says "town" so that the gates are not taken to be garden gates; Deuteronomy's "your gates" are the gates of the towns where Israel will live (12:15).

source.text: לְמַ֨עַן יִרְבּ֤וּ יְמֵיכֶם֙ וִימֵ֣י בְנֵיכֶ֔ם עַ֚ל הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֧ע יְהוָ֛ה לַאֲבֹתֵיכֶ֖ם לָתֵ֣ת לָהֶ֑ם כִּימֵ֥י הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם עַל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: so that may be many your days and [the] days of your sons on the land which swore Yahweh to your fathers to give to them, like [the] days of the heavens above the earth.

en.L: so that your days and the days of your {{gender:children|sons}} may be many on the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your fathers to give to them, like the days of the heavens above the earth.
en.B: so that you and your {{gender:children|sons}} may live long in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} swore to your ancestors to give them, as long as the sky remains above the earth.
en.R: Then you and your {{gender:children|sons}} will live a long time in the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} promised with an oath to give your ancestors. You will live there as long as the sky is above the earth.

decisions.choice: like the days of the heavens above the earth: for all time
decisions.reason: The sky over the earth stands for what lasts. Israel may live in the land as long as the heavens last, that is for ever (compare Psalm 89:30).

decisions.choice: to give to them: to the fathers themselves
decisions.reason: The land was promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob themselves (Genesis 13:15; 26:3; 28:13), and they are counted as receiving it in their descendants.

decisions.choice: you and your children may live long
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "you and your children live long" for "your days and the days of your children be many", as "prolong days" in verse 9.

source.text: כִּי֩ אִם־שָׁמֹ֨ר תִּשְׁמְר֜וּן אֶת־כָּל־הַמִּצְוָ֣ה הַזֹּ֗את אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם לַעֲשֹׂתָ֑הּ לְאַהֲבָ֞ה אֶת־יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֛ם לָלֶ֥כֶת בְּכָל־דְּרָכָ֖יו וּלְדָבְקָה־בֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For if surely you will keep all the commandment this which I [am] commanding you to do it, to love Yahweh your God, to walk in all his ways, and to cling to him,

en.L: For if you will carefully keep all this commandment that I am commanding you to do it, to love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, to walk in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, and to cling to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
en.B: For if you carefully keep this whole commandment that I am giving you to follow, loving {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, walking in all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} ways, and holding fast to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
en.R: Carefully obey all these commands I am giving you. Love {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, live the way {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wants you to live, and stay close to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: surely keep: keep carefully, in earnest
decisions.reason: The verb "keep" is doubled for emphasis, as "listen" is in verse 13.

decisions.choice: walk in all his ways: live as he directs
decisions.reason: Life is pictured as a road; to walk in God's ways is to live by his commands (8:6; 10:12).

decisions.choice: cling to him: hold fast to him in loyalty
decisions.reason: The verb means to stick or hold fast. It describes a husband joined to his wife (Genesis 2:24) and Ruth clinging to Naomi (Ruth 1:14); here it is loyal attachment to the LORD alone (10:20; 13:5).

decisions.choice: Carefully obey ... (commands, with the condition picked up in verse 23)
decisions.reason: As in verse 13, Readable turns the "if" clause into commands and picks up the condition in verse 23 ("If you do").

source.text: וְהוֹרִ֧ישׁ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֥ם הָאֵ֖לֶּה מִלִּפְנֵיכֶ֑ם וִֽירִשְׁתֶּ֣ם גּוֹיִ֔ם גְּדֹלִ֥ים וַעֲצֻמִ֖ים מִכֶּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and will dispossess Yahweh all the nations these from before you, and you will dispossess nations great and mighty more than you.

en.L: then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will drive out all these nations from before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and mightier than you.
en.B: then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will drive out all these nations ahead of you, and you will dispossess nations greater and stronger than you are.
en.R: If you do, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will drive out all these nations as you advance. You will take over the land of nations that are bigger and stronger than you.

decisions.choice: drive out ... dispossess: the LORD removes the nations, and Israel takes their place
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice in two forms: the LORD makes the nations lose their land, and Israel takes it over from them. The victory is the LORD's work, carried out through Israel (9:1-3).

decisions.choice: nations greater and mightier than you: as in 4:38, 7:1 and 9:1
decisions.reason: Moses repeats that Israel will not win the land by its own size or strength.

decisions.choice: take over the land of nations
decisions.reason: Readable says what dispossessing a nation means: taking over its land.

source.text: כָּל־הַמָּק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּדְרֹ֧ךְ כַּֽף־רַגְלְכֶ֛ם בּ֖וֹ לָכֶ֣ם יִהְיֶ֑ה מִן־הַמִּדְבָּ֨ר וְהַלְּבָנ֜וֹן מִן־הַנָּהָ֣ר נְהַר־פְּרָ֗ת וְעַד֙ הַיָּ֣ם הָֽאַחֲר֔וֹן יִהְיֶ֖ה גְּבֻלְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Every the place which will tread [the] sole of your foot on it, to you it will be; from the wilderness and the Lebanon, from the river, [the] river Euphrates, and to the sea the western will be your territory.

en.L: Every place on which the sole of your foot treads shall be yours. From the wilderness and the Lebanon, from the River, the river Euphrates, as far as the western sea shall be your territory.
en.B: Every place where you set foot will be yours. Your territory will reach from the wilderness to Lebanon, and from the River, the Euphrates, to the western sea.
en.R: Every place you walk on will be yours. Your land will reach from the desert in the south to the mountains of Lebanon in the north, and from the Euphrates River in the east to the Mediterranean Sea in the west.

decisions.choice: every place the sole of your foot treads: every place you go into and claim
decisions.reason: To set foot on land is to enter it and take hold of it. The LORD repeats the promise to Joshua in the same words (Joshua 1:3).

decisions.choice: the borders: the southern wilderness, Lebanon in the north, the Euphrates, the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: The wilderness is the dry land to the south, toward Sinai; Lebanon is the mountain range to the north; "the River" is the Euphrates, far to the north-east; and "the western sea" (literally "the sea behind", since west lay behind someone facing east) is the Mediterranean. The same borders are given in Genesis 15:18 and Joshua 1:4. Israel's rule reached this far only under David and Solomon (1 Kings 5:1, 4).

decisions.choice: from the wilderness and Lebanon: two limits, south and north
decisions.reason: The Hebrew lists "from the wilderness and the Lebanon" side by side, then "from the River ... to the western sea". The first pair gives the southern and northern limits, the second the eastern and western.

decisions.choice: in the south ... in the north ... in the east ... in the west; the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: Readable adds the directions and the modern name of the sea, following meaning decisions m2 and m3.

source.text: לֹא־יִתְיַצֵּ֥ב אִ֖ישׁ בִּפְנֵיכֶ֑ם פַּחְדְּכֶ֨ם וּמֽוֹרַאֲכֶ֜ם יִתֵּ֣ן׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֗ם עַל־פְּנֵ֤י כָל־הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּדְרְכוּ־בָ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר לָכֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Not will stand a man before you; your dread and your fear will put Yahweh your God on [the] face of all the land which you will tread on it, as he spoke to you.

en.L: {{gender:No one|No man}} will stand before you; the dread of you and the fear of you {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God will put on the face of all the land on which you tread, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to you.
en.B: {{gender:No one|No man}} will be able to stand against you. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will put the dread and fear of you on the whole land where you set foot, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised you.
en.R: {{gender:No one|No man}} will be able to stand up to you. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will make the people afraid of you everywhere you go in the land, just as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} promised.

decisions.choice: stand before you: hold out against you
decisions.reason: To "stand before" an enemy is to resist and hold one's ground (7:24; Joshua 1:5).

decisions.choice: your dread and your fear: the dread and fear others will have of you
decisions.reason: "Your" here means the fear felt toward Israel, not Israel's own fear, as in 2:25.

decisions.choice: as he spoke to you: the promise of Exodus 23:27
decisions.reason: The LORD had promised to send terror ahead of Israel and throw its enemies into confusion (Exodus 23:27; Deuteronomy 2:25).

decisions.choice: a man: anyone at all
decisions.reason: The word is "man", but the sense is "no one".

decisions.choice: make the people afraid of you
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what putting dread on the land means: the people living there will be afraid.

source.text: רְאֵ֗ה אָנֹכִ֛י נֹתֵ֥ן לִפְנֵיכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם בְּרָכָ֖ה וּקְלָלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: See, I [am] setting before you today a blessing and a curse:

en.L: See, I am setting before you today a blessing and a curse:
en.B: See, I am setting before you today a blessing and a curse:
en.R: Listen! Today I am giving you a choice between a blessing and a curse.

decisions.choice: a blessing and a curse: the two outcomes of the covenant
decisions.reason: Blessing is life and plenty in the land under God's favor; curse is the loss of them. Which one comes depends on Israel's obedience (verses 27-28). The theme returns in the ceremony of 27:11-26, the blessings and curses of chapter 28, and the final call to choose in 30:15-19.

decisions.choice: See ... before you: one people addressed both as one and as many
decisions.reason: "See" is singular and "before you" is plural. Deuteronomy often moves between the two: Israel is spoken to as one nation and as its many members.

decisions.choice: a choice between
decisions.reason: Readable says that the blessing and curse are set before Israel to choose between, as verses 27-28 explain and 30:19 says outright. "See" becomes "Listen!", the ordinary way to call attention in plain English.

source.text: אֶֽת־הַבְּרָכָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּשְׁמְע֗וּ אֶל־מִצְוֺת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: the blessing, that you will listen to [the] commandments of Yahweh your God which I [am] commanding you today,

en.L: the blessing, if you listen to the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I am commanding you today,
en.B: the blessing if you obey the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I am giving you today,
en.R: You will be blessed if you obey the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God that I am giving you today.

decisions.choice: that you will listen: if, on condition that you obey
decisions.reason: The word normally means "which" or "that"; here it introduces the condition for the blessing, matching the "if" for the curse in verse 28.

decisions.choice: listen to the commandments: obey them
decisions.reason: To listen to commands is to do them, as in verse 13.

source.text: וְהַקְּלָלָ֗ה אִם־לֹ֤א תִשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶל־מִצְוֺת֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וְסַרְתֶּ֣ם מִן־הַדֶּ֔רֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י מְצַוֶּ֥ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם הַיּ֑וֹם לָלֶ֗כֶת אַחֲרֵ֛י אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֲחֵרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יְדַעְתֶּֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and the curse, if not you will listen to [the] commandments of Yahweh your God, and you turn aside from the way which I [am] commanding you today, to go after other gods which you have not known.

en.L: and the curse, if you do not listen to the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and turn aside from the way that I am commanding you today, to go after other gods that you have not known.
en.B: and the curse if you do not obey the commandments of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, but turn aside from the way I am commanding you today and follow other gods that you have not known.
en.R: But you will be cursed if you do not obey the commands of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You will be cursed if you turn away from the path I am showing you today and follow other gods that you have never known.

decisions.choice: go after other gods: follow them, worship them
decisions.reason: To walk after a god is to be its follower and worshiper (6:14; 8:19).

decisions.choice: gods you have not known: gods with whom you have no history
decisions.reason: Israel has known the LORD by what he did before their eyes (verses 2-7). The other gods have done nothing for them; they are strangers (13:3, 7; 32:17).

decisions.choice: the way that I am commanding you: the path of life the commandments mark out
decisions.reason: Life is pictured as a road, and the commands mark the way to walk in (5:33; 9:12, 16). To turn aside from it is to leave the LORD.

decisions.choice: the path I am showing you
decisions.reason: Readable says "showing" rather than "commanding" with "path", which reads more naturally in plain English; the path is the one Moses commands.

decisions.choice: You will be cursed if ... (repeated)
decisions.reason: Readable splits the two conditions into two sentences and repeats "you will be cursed" for clarity.

source.text: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּ֤י יְבִֽיאֲךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ אֶל־הָאָ֕רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־אַתָּ֥ה בָא־שָׁ֖מָּה לְרִשְׁתָּ֑הּ וְנָתַתָּ֤ה אֶת־הַבְּרָכָה֙ עַל־הַ֣ר גְּרִזִ֔ים וְאֶת־הַקְּלָלָ֖ה עַל־הַ֥ר עֵיבָֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be, when brings you Yahweh your God into the land which you [are] going there to possess it, and you will set the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.

en.L: And it shall be, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God brings you into the land that you are entering to take possession of it, that you shall put the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
en.B: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess, you are to proclaim the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God will bring you into the land you are going to take over. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does, you must announce the blessing from Mount Gerizim and the curse from Mount Ebal.

decisions.choice: set the blessing on: proclaim it from that mountain
decisions.reason: The verb is "give" or "put". The ceremony is described in 27:11-26 and carried out in Joshua 8:30-35: half the tribes stood on Gerizim for the blessing, half on Ebal for the curse, and the words were read aloud.

decisions.choice: Gerizim and Ebal: two mountains facing each other at Shechem
decisions.reason: The two mountains stand on either side of the valley of Shechem, in the middle of the land: Gerizim to the south, Ebal to the north. Shechem is where Abram first built an altar in the land (Genesis 12:6-7).

decisions.choice: proclaim (Balanced); announce ... from (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "putting" the blessing on a mountain means, following meaning decision m1; Literal keeps "put".

source.text: הֲלֹא־הֵ֜מָּה בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֗ן אַֽחֲרֵי֙ דֶּ֚רֶךְ מְב֣וֹא הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ בְּאֶ֨רֶץ֙ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י הַיֹּשֵׁ֖ב בָּעֲרָבָ֑ה מ֚וּל הַגִּלְגָּ֔ל אֵ֖צֶל אֵלוֹנֵ֥י מֹרֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: [Are] not they across the Jordan, behind [the] way of [the] going in of the sun, in [the] land of the Canaanite who dwells in the Arabah, opposite the Gilgal, beside [the] oaks of Moreh?

en.L: [Are] they not across the Jordan, beyond the road of the going down of the sun, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
en.B: Are they not across the Jordan, beyond the road toward the sunset, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, facing Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
en.R: As you know, these mountains are on the other side of the Jordan River. They are past the western road, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Jordan Valley. They are across from Gilgal, near the oaks of Moreh.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan: here the west side, seen from where Moses stands
decisions.reason: Moses speaks in Moab, east of the river (1:5). The mountains lie on the other side from him, to the west, in the land Israel is about to enter. Elsewhere in the book the same phrase can name the east side, seen from the land (1:1).

decisions.choice: beyond the road of the setting sun: west of a main road, or along the road going west
decisions.reason: The phrase is unclear. It may name a known road running north and south, with the mountains west of it, or the road that goes west, toward the sunset, from the Jordan up into the hills.

decisions.choice: the Arabah, Gilgal and the oaks of Moreh
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the deep valley of the Jordan, here standing for the land of Canaan around it. The oaks of Moreh were near Shechem, where Abram stopped when he first came into the land (Genesis 12:6). Which Gilgal is meant is not certain: it may be the camp near Jericho (Joshua 4:19), which would make the description a general one, or another place of the same name near Shechem; the name means "circle" and was given to more than one place.

decisions.choice: Are they not ...?: a question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The question reminds the hearers of something they know: these mountains are in the land west of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: As you know ...; the Jordan Valley
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies and calls the Arabah "the Jordan Valley".

source.text: כִּ֤י אַתֶּם֙ עֹבְרִ֣ים אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֔ן לָבֹא֙ לָרֶ֣שֶׁת אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם נֹתֵ֣ן לָכֶ֑ם וִֽירִשְׁתֶּ֥ם אֹתָ֖הּ וִֽישַׁבְתֶּם־בָּֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For you [are] crossing the Jordan to go in to possess the land which Yahweh your God [is] giving to you, and you will possess it and dwell in it,

en.L: For you are crossing the Jordan to go in to take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving to you, and you will take possession of it and live in it,
en.B: For you are about to cross the Jordan to go in and take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you. When you have taken possession of it and are living in it,
en.R: You are about to cross the Jordan River to go in and take over the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving you. When you have taken it and are living there,

decisions.choice: you are crossing: you are about to cross
decisions.reason: The participle describes what is about to happen: Israel stands at the river, ready to cross (9:1).

decisions.choice: you will possess it and live in it: once settled, you still must obey
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 32: when the land is theirs and they are living in it, they are still to be careful to keep the laws. Possessing the land is not the end of obedience but the setting for it.

source.text: וּשְׁמַרְתֶּ֣ם לַעֲשׂ֔וֹת אֵ֥ת כָּל־הַֽחֻקִּ֖ים וְאֶת־הַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר אָנֹכִ֛י נֹתֵ֥ן לִפְנֵיכֶ֖ם הַיּֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will keep to do all the statutes and the judgments which I [am] setting before you today.

en.L: and you shall be careful to do all the statutes and the judgments that I am setting before you today.
en.B: be careful to carry out all the statutes and rulings that I am setting before you today.
en.R: be careful to obey all the laws and rules I am giving you today.

decisions.choice: the statutes and the judgments: the laws about to be given in chapters 12-26
decisions.reason: The words close the long opening of Moses' speech (5:1 to 11:32) and lead straight into 12:1, "These are the statutes and the judgments", where the detailed laws begin.

decisions.choice: setting before you: as the blessing and curse are set before you
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used in verse 26. In setting the laws before Israel, Moses also sets before them the choice between blessing and curse.

decisions.choice: statutes and judgments (Literal); statutes and rulings (Balanced); laws and rules (Readable)
decisions.reason: These are the settled renderings for these two words in Deuteronomy. Verse 1 lists them in the same way.
